questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I like bread made up of corn ________.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I like bread made up of corn ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'flour'.
 
Key Points
  • The word "flour" refers to a powder obtained by grinding grain, typically wheat, and used to make bread, cakes, and pastry. (आटा)
  • It is the correct ingredient used to make bread.
  • The other options: "flower," "floor," and "failure" do not fit the context of making bread.

​Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2'.

Complete Sentence: I like bread made up of corn flour.

Additional Information
  • Flower (फूल): The reproductive structure found in flowering plants (plants of the division Magnoliophyta, also called angiosperms).
  • Floor (मंजिल): The lower surface of a room, on which one may walk.
  • Failure (असफलता): Lack of success.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. Verity is a good virtue for human life.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.

Verity is a good virtue for human life.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2.

Key Points

  • The word "verity" means the quality of being true or real; it denotes something that is true or an established truth. (सत्यता)
    • Example: She had always believed in the verity of his statements.
  • "Truth" refers to the quality or state of being true; it is a fact or belief that is accepted as true. (सत्य)
    • Example: The truth about the incident was finally revealed in the investigation.
  • Hence, we can infer that 'verity' is synonymous with 'truth'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Knowledge (ज्ञान): Information, understanding, or skill that you get from experience or education.
    • Example: His knowledge of history is impressive.

    • Example: We received new information about the case.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. Founding father / is / of / New Historicism / Greenblatt / considered / the.

Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

Founding father / is / of / New Historicism / Greenblatt / considered / the.

options.text: The founding father of New Historicism is considered Greenblatt.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate verb / verb phrase to fill in the blank. The team __________ the championship before their star player got injured.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate verb / verb phrase to fill in the blank.
The team __________ the championship before their star player got injured.
questions.solution:
```html

The correct answer is 'had won' i.e. this part of the sentence is correct.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the use of the past perfect tense 'had won' is correct as it indicates an action that was completed before another action in the past (the star player got injured).
  • The past perfect tense is used to show that an action was completed before another action in the past.
  • Therefore, the past perfect form of the verb 'had won' is used correctly in this context.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: The team had won the championship before their star player got injured.

Additional Information

  • The past perfect tense is often used in sentences to show a sequence of past events, where one event occurred before the other.
    • Example: By the time we arrived at the station, the train had left.
  • It is important to use the correct tense to convey the intended meaning and timeline of events accurately.
    • Example: She had finished her homework before she went out to play.
```

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A.He remembered her as she once was – an eager, glowing girl. B.He had not seen her for nearly thirteen years. C.Mr. Satterthwaite went to meet her. D.And now he saw – a Frozen Lady.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful
and coherent paragraph.
A.He remembered her as she once was – an eager, glowing girl.
B.He had not seen her for nearly thirteen years.
C.Mr. Satterthwaite went to meet her.
D.And now he saw – a Frozen Lady.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
Key Points
  • The paragraph revolves around Mr. Satterthwaite and his observations upon meeting a lady after many years.
  • Sentence C is the first sentence as it introduces Mr. Satterthwaite's action of going to meet her:
    • "Mr. Satterthwaite went to meet her."
  • Sentence B follows next to provide context about the long gap in their meeting:
    • "He had not seen her for nearly thirteen years."
  • Sentence A is the third sentence as it gives his past memory of her:
    • "He remembered her as she once was – an eager, glowing girl."
  • Sentence D comes last as it contrasts the present state with his memory:
    • "And now he saw – a Frozen Lady."
  • The correct sequence is CBAD.
 
Coherent paragraph after rearrangement:
"Mr. Satterthwaite went to meet her. He had not seen her for nearly thirteen years. He remembered her as she once was – an eager, glowing girl. And now he saw – a Frozen Lady."

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice. Gill scored 3 centuries in Tata IPL 2023
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.
Gill scored 3 centuries in Tata IPL 2023

options.text: 3 centuries has been scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023.
options.html: 3 centuries has been scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023.

options.text: 3 centuries were scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023.
options.html: 3 centuries were scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023.

options.text: 3 centuries had been scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023.
options.html: 3 centuries had been scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023.

options.text: 3 centuries were being scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023.
options.html: 3 centuries were being scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: "Gill scored 3 centuries in Tata IPL 2023."
  • To convert to passive voice: Place the object "3 centuries" at the beginning.
  • Change the active verb form "scored" to "were scored" (past simple passive).
  • Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "Gill."
  • Ensure the time phrase "in Tata IPL 2023" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
 
Correct Sentence: "3 centuries were scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "3 centuries has been scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023." – Incorrect verb form (singular instead of plural).
  • Option 3: "3 centuries had been scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023." – Incorrect tense (past perfect passive).
  • Option 4: "3 centuries were being scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023." – Incorrect aspect (past continuous passive).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'frequently'.
 
Key Points
  • The passage discusses how social media companies claim to promote democracy and empower individuals.
  • The word to fill in blank number 1 should indicate how often these claims are made by social media companies.
  • "Frequently" fits best as it means that these companies often make such claims, aligning with the context of the passage.
  • Other options like "seldom", "never", and "don't" do not fit the logical context of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'frequently'.
 
Complete Passage: Social media companies (1) frequently claim that they promote democracy and are dedicated to the empowerment of ordinary individuals. The assertion (2) ______ entirely unfounded. Recent history shows how (3) ______ citizens have been mobilised against totalitarian regimes on social networking sites. Starting from MeToo to Black Lives Matter, digital networks (4) ______ indispensable in bringing together critical voices against social and political (5) ______.
 
Additional Information
  • Seldom: Means rarely, which does not align with the idea that social media companies often make these claims.
  • Never: Means not at all, which contradicts the passage's context of these claims being made.
  • Don't: Grammatically incorrect in this context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'may not be'.
Key Points
  • The passage discusses the claims made by social media companies about promoting democracy and empowerment.
  • The assertion mentioned in the passage is being questioned in terms of its validity.
  • "May not be" fits best as it suggests doubt about the assertion being entirely unfounded, which aligns with the context.
  • Other options like "cannot", "should", and "shall" do not fit the context of expressing doubt or questioning validity.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'may not be'.
 
Complete Passage: Social media companies (1) frequently claim that they promote democracy and are dedicated to the empowerment of ordinary individuals. The assertion (2) may not be entirely unfounded. Recent history shows how (3) ______ citizens have been mobilised against totalitarian regimes on social networking sites. Starting from MeToo to Black Lives Matter, digital networks (4) ______ indispensable in bringing together critical voices against social and political (5) ______.
 
Additional Information
  • Cannot: Implies a strong negation, which doesn’t fit the context of merely questioning the assertion.
  • Should: Implies a recommendation or advice, which does not fit the context.
  • Shall: Implies a definitive future action, which does not fit the context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.

Key Points

Complete Passage: Social media companies (1) frequently claim that they promote democracy and are dedicated to the empowerment of ordinary individuals. The assertion (2) may not be entirely unfounded. Recent history shows how (3) common citizens have been mobilised against totalitarian regimes on social networking sites. Starting from MeToo to Black Lives Matter, digital networks (4) ______ indispensable in bringing together critical voices against social and political (5) ______.
 
Additional Information
  • Alien: Implies something foreign or unfamiliar, which does not fit the context of typical citizens being mobilized.
  • Neutral: Implies a lack of involvement, which does not fit the context of active citizen mobilization.
  • Foreign: Implies something from another country, which does not fit the context of the passage.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'have been'.
 
Key Points
  • The passage discusses the role of digital networks in recent history, emphasizing their essential nature.
  • The word to fill in blank number 4 should describe the past and ongoing role of digital networks.
  • "Have been" fits best as it suggests that digital networks have continued to be indispensable over time, aligning with the context of the passage.
  • Other options like "can", "were", and "that" do not fit as well because they do not convey the ongoing and continued importance of digital networks.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'have been'.
 
Complete Passage: Social media companies (1) frequently claim that they promote democracy and are dedicated to the empowerment of ordinary individuals. The assertion (2) may not be entirely unfounded. Recent history shows how (3) common citizens have been mobilised against totalitarian regimes on social networking sites. Starting from MeToo to Black Lives Matter, digital networks (4) have been indispensable in bringing together critical voices against social and political (5) ______.
 
Additional Information
  • Can: Implies potential but does not convey the ongoing and past importance of digital networks.
